texts.label: text
texts.orig: Held annually since 2015, WAAW is a global campaign that aims to raise awareness of antimicrobial resistance worldwide and encourage best practices among the general public, health workers and policy makers to slow the development and spread of drug-resistant infections. texts.label: text
texts.orig: AMR occurs  naturally  usually  through  genetic  changes.  Antimicrobial  resistant organisms are found in people, animals, food, plants and the environment (in water, soil and air). They can spread from person to person or between people and animals, including from food of animal origin. The main drivers of antimicrobial resistance include the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials; lack of access to clean water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) for both humans and animals; poor infection and disease prevention and control in health-care facilities and farms; poor access to quality, affordable medicines, vaccines and diagnostics; lack of awareness and knowledge.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Kenya has done a lot towards reduction of Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR). Kenya was among the first countries to develop a National AMR Action Plan (NAP), an AMR policy, an AMR communication Strategy and NAP monitoring and evaluation framework. Kenya has done a lot of awareness creation on AMR targeting the public, journalists and even the policy makers. The Kenyan model is being replicat -ed in other countries across the world.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Codex Alimentarius Commission (CAC) is a Latin word for 'Food Code', is a collection of standards, guidelines and codes of practice that governments may opt to use to ensure food safety, quality and fair trade. It comprises of a series of general and specific food safety standards that have been formulated with objec -tive of protecting consumers' health and ensuring fair practices in food trade. CAC was formed in 1963 by two United Nations Organizations (FAO and WHO) and its headquarters is in Rome, Italy.

texts.label: text

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The awareness on the pests and diseases in bee colonies  by  farmers  is  key  towards  maintaining honey bee health. Keeping bee colonies free from pests and diseases require that the beekeepers are knowledgeable  on  bee  pests  and  diseases.  To assess this the section used  self-administered questionnaires in Kwale and Kilifi counties.

Keeping bee colonies free from pests and diseases require that the beekeepers are knowledgeable  on  bee  pests  and  diseases.  To assess this the section used  self-administered questionnaires in Kwale and Kilifi counties.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: It  emerged that a majority of farmers in the two counties had very little knowledge on honey bee pests and diseases. Most of them lacked tools for managing their hives such as bee suits and this negatively affected their level of productivity. Knowledge in notifiable diseases and pests such as American foul brood, European foul brood and varroa mites was found to be low or lacking and therefore affecting the quality of their honey and other bee hive products for the international markets.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This Bill builds on the Meat Control Act Cap. 356. While initially the onus was on the DVS this Bill seeks to transfer some public health responsibilities to the food businesses operators to fully operationalize the farm to folk principle as applied in veterinary public health. Through this Bill the DVS will audit farms producing foods of animal origin; this approach will ensure antimicrobial residues; aflatoxins are reduced right from the source.
